title: HyperSVG 2.0 capability media: Recorded media
description: a media binding (door 2 draws, D31): {"target": "<video region>", "media": {"video", "fit", "focal", "autoplay", "stallMs", "markers"}}, with the binding's id and label beside target; the calls media.play, media.pause {place} and media.seek {place, atMs} | a resource kind video (2.6): a local file, MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio, or WebM with VP9 video and Opus audio, with durationMs (at most 86,400,000, 24 hours), width, height and digest; at most 64 MiB per file, and 256 MiB for all video members of a package (10.8); a videoBytes budget (A10.3) may only lower this; an optional poster (an image resource id) and captions (a map from a language tag to a captions resource id); a captions resource is WebVTT, one file per language, with a language | a drawn place: an unpainted rect with data-hsvg-fit="video" (5.10); it shows the video resource that a media binding names | the media binding's video (6.8): a formula giving a video resource id for the place named by target; the video is shown with contain by default, and the media binding may give fit "cover" with an optional focal [x, y] from 0 to 1 (7.5); a video starts paused and may start by itself with autoplay true, which starts with sound forced off; under reduced motion the video stays paused on its poster; the binding may give a label (the place's accessible name, beside target) and the media binding stallMs (integer 1000..60000, default 10000); the media binding may list markers, up to 256 {id, atMs, event}, by time like clip markers; a marker fires only when the video's time crosses atMs going forward; a marker past its video's durationMs is E-RANGE | the capability actions media.play, media.pause and media.seek, each naming the place; media.seek also takes atMs, a formula giving a time in the video, proven from 0 to the largest durationMs of the videos the binding can show (E-RANGE), and doing nothing when no video is bound; an unmuted media.play needs a trusted person activation, and if the browser refuses it the video stays paused and the action ends with ended:<id> {failed: true} | the events media:ended:<place>, when the video reaches its end, media:stalled:<place>, when it stops for lack of data, and media:failed:<place>, when it cannot load, cannot decode or has stalled longer than stallMs; all carry {atMs}, the time in the video | the video follows the local clock of the scene that shows it, at that clock's speed; a stall adds the pause reason buffering (3.10), and time moves again when the video can play and every other reason has cleared; a stall longer than stallMs removes the buffering reason and fires media:failed:<place>; when the video is more than 250 ms off the scene clock, the player re-seeks it | captions in the active language are shown and announced like spoken lines (6.11); the video's sound follows muted and volume (5.5) | an export that cannot carry video reports each video resource in notCarried (A10.1) | privileged capability (10.7): the engine checks the ports it uses against the experience's grants; it needs no grant of its own, because a video is always a local file in the package (2.6)
